info.title: API.SH: Finviz
info.description: The Finviz API from API.SH: public Finviz data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.summary: Fetch a past response again, free
get.description: The exact response a call returned, for 30 days after the call, at no cost. Use the call's x-request-id. Supports output=csv|ndjson.

200.description: The stored response (headers: x-refetch: 1, x-original-time, x-original-route).

404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

get.description:
US economic releases for a date range (default: this week): date and Eastern time, event, category, reference period, actual, forecast, model forecast, previous value, importance (1-3) and whether a higher number is good. Filter by minimum importance or words.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/finviz-calendar

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: First day (YYYY-MM-DD); default this Monday.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: Last day (YYYY-MM-DD), up to 31 days after date_from.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: One day instead of a range.

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Keep releases of at least this importance (1 low, 2 medium, 3 high).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words in the event or category name, e.g. payrolls.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Times are US Eastern. importance: 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high.

get.description:
Sort by any column and page through busy days.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/finviz-earnings

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Day to list, YYYY-MM-DD (past or upcoming). Default: today in New York, or the last Friday at a weekend.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: earningsDate (default), ticker, company, marketCap, epsEstimate, epsActual, epsSurprise, salesEstimate, salesActual, salesSurprise or oneDayPriceReaction; prefix - for descending.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, 50 reports per page (default 1). `next_page` is null on the last page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Market cap, EPS and sales are as Finviz shows them (market cap and sales in millions of USD).

get.summary: Finviz sector, industry and country performance
get.description:
Group performance tables for US-listed stocks by sector, industry (all, or within one sector), country or market-cap class. The views carry performance over a week, month, quarter, half year, year and year to date with volume, relative volume and the day's change; or market cap, dividend, P/E, forward P/E, PEG, debt ratios and short float; or valuation multiples and growth; or returns, liquidity ratios and margins. Values come as shown and as plain numbers, with the screener filter of each group.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/finviz-groups

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: sector (default), industry, country or capitalization.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: performance (default), overview, valuation or financial.

parameters.name: sector
parameters.description: With `group=industry`, only the industries of this sector.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort column such as name, marketcap, pe, forwardpe, dividendyield; prefix - for descending, for example -marketcap.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Market cap and volume are as Finviz shows them (B = billions, M = millions); `numbers` holds the same values as plain numbers. `filter` can …

get.description:
The values behind Finviz's market heat maps: every ticker's performance (1 day to 1 year, year to date) or metric (relative volume, P/E, forward P/E, PEG, P/S, P/B, dividend %, EPS growth, short float, analyst recommendation, days to earnings) for the S&P 500, all US stocks, Dow, Nasdaq 100, Russell 2000, Nasdaq Composite, world ADRs or ETFs, with how many are up and down and, for the sector and world maps, each sector's or country's value.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/finviz-map

get.description:
Finviz's stock screener with every column for each match (about 115 fields: descriptive, valuation, growth, margins, ownership, short interest, performance, technicals and the latest headline). Filter with Finviz filter codes, a signal, or a ticker list, sorted by any column. 20 a page; pass `next_page` back as `page`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/finviz-screener

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Comma-separated Finviz filter codes (see /finviz/v1/screener-filters; codes from finviz.com URLs such as fa_pe_u20 or ta_rsi_os30 work too).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort column code, '-' for descending (marketcap, price, change, volume, pe, dividendyield, perf4w ...).

parameters.name: signal
parameters.description: A Finviz signal such as ta_topgainers, ta_toplosers, ta_newhigh, ta_unusualvolume, ta_mostactive.

parameters.name: tickers
parameters.description: Only these tickers, comma-separated.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Market cap, income, sales and share counts are in millions, as Finviz shows them.

items.wiimDailyDigest: Apple begins Apple Intelligence trial rollout in China, confirms Alibaba Qwen partnership ahead of December public launch

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Pass option values comma-separated as `filters` (e.g. cap_largeover,sec_technology). Fundamental and technical filter codes from finviz.com …

items.name: Exchange
items.description: Stock Exchange where a stock is listed.

items.name: Index
items.description: Major market Index that includes the stock.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
